messages.organization: Civic Works — Center for Sustainable Careers
messages.contactRole: Center for Sustainable Careers — Employer/Training team
messages.subject: A live Maryland solar jobs feed for Civic Works
messages.body:
Hi Civic Works team,

I’m Bassem, founder of Solar Roles, a U.S. job platform focused exclusively on solar careers.

I came across Civic Works’ Center for Sustainable Careers and its long-running hands-on solar installer training and placement work.

We recently built a free solar jobs widget for schools and workforce programs. For Civic Works, it can be preloaded to show current solar openings in Maryland by default, so participants can see relevant opportunities without starting a separate job search.

It updates automatically as openings enter and leave the database, and the standard embed requires no account or subscription.

You can see it here:
https://www.solarroles.com/workforce-resources/jobs-widget?state=MD&limit=6

I thought it could fit naturally alongside the employment resources you already provide participants. If it looks useful, you’re welcome to embed it or share the link directly.
messages.sourceSuggestedPitchAngle: Long-running solar installer workforce program with hands-on installation/electrical training and employer placement support. Strong direct resource-link target.

messages.subject: New Hampshire solar hiring data for Clean Energy New Hampshire
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

My name is Bassem — I founded Solar Roles, a U.S. platform focused on solar jobs and workforce resources.

Clean Energy New Hampshire already publishes career information and connects employers and workers across the state, so a live New Hampshire solar hiring snapshot seemed like a natural fit.

We recently published a live 50-state Solar Job Market resource built from active indexed postings. For New Hampshire, it gives a current view of active postings and explicitly entry-level openings. The data refreshes daily, which makes it useful as a current workforce snapshot rather than a static annual report.

You can see it here:
https://www.solarroles.com/workforce-resources/solar-job-market-by-state

I thought it could be useful as a resource-page or newsletter reference for people following the local solar workforce.
messages.sourceSuggestedPitchAngle: They publish clean-energy career information and connect the state ecosystem; offer New Hampshire solar demand and career-pathway resources.
